    Thin directed categories and the extension of multiplicative bases #

    Abstract form of Subsection 4.4 (scalar-normalization.tex). A k-linear category is thin if its Hom spaces have dimension at most one, its endomorphisms are scalars, and it is directed (no nonzero morphisms both ways between distinct objects). A multiplicative basis on a set of objects chooses a nonzero vector on each nonzero line, identities on objects, and is closed under composition up to zero.

    Lemma 4.11(1) (lem:source-basis-extension): a multiplicative basis on a finite set extends over a source. The proof is the source's: choose f_y in T(s, y), write f_y b_{yz} = μ_{yz} f_z, express μ through object values by Lemma 4.9 on the support poset of Lemma 4.10, and rescale the f_y. The representation-finiteness of the incidence algebra of the support poset is a hypothesis here; it is supplied by Lemma 4.10 for the graded covering category (SupportPoset.lean). Sinks are sources of the opposite category.
